conceptZh: 玩具機器人專心拿刷子作畫，刷子卡住後突然彈回來，在他自己臉上刷出一撇翹鬍子；他愣了一下，照照小鏡子，反而超滿意地摸摸鬍子鞠了個躬。
object: a toy robot artist with an oversized paintbrush
morph: the glyph 畫 stands still as a solid sculpture while the paintbrush gag plays out beside it
creativeAngle: 連到孩子喜歡的漫威與漫畫：笑點是「刷子反彈畫了自己一臉鬍子，本人卻覺得很帥」，用得意的反應取代出糗，情緒是正向的。畫十二畫且橫畫多、最容易糊在一起，所以讓字體靜止並特別要求橫畫等距。語音詞「漫畫」，漫ㄇㄢˋ、畫ㄏㄨㄚˋ都是單一讀音。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale butter cream background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 畫 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep indigo, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the brush-shaped 聿 on top, the 田 in the middle and the wide flat base below stay clearly separated, with every horizontal stroke evenly spaced and never touching. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. Beside its lower left stands a small toy robot artist wearing a tiny beret, gripping a paintbrush twice his own height. From 0.6 seconds he works with enormous concentration, tongue out, dabbing carefully at the air in front of him, leaning in closer and closer. At 2.0 seconds the brush catches on something, bends back like a bow, and he tugs harder and harder with both hands. At 2.7 seconds it springs free and whips around, sweeping one bold curly moustache right across his own face. He freezes, cross-eyed. Beat. At 3.5 seconds he pulls out a tiny mirror, looks, and instead of panicking he strokes the moustache, delighted, then takes a small proud bow towards the camera and struts out of frame to the left by 4.6 seconds. From 4.7 seconds to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 畫 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「畫、畫、漫畫」, using the reading ㄏㄨㄚˋ for 畫 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 畫 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 漫畫 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 畫: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 小手拿不到蠟筆的橡膠恐龍，改用大腳作畫，滑了一跤卻漂亮地完成「畫」字最下面的一橫。
object: An original rubber dinosaur with enormous feet, impossibly tiny arms, and one indigo crayon.
morph: The dinosaur uses a crayon held between its toes to draw the glyph’s final bottom horizontal stroke; every other stroke is already in its correct position.
creativeAngle: 把短手與大腳的反差直接變成作畫笑點：恐龍伸手屢次落空，換腳握筆卻滑成坐姿，意外畫出漂亮的一橫。最後一筆依正確字形完成，笑點不改動筆畫。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation in one locked, front-facing shot. On a pale warm apricot drawing surface, center one Traditional Chinese target glyph, 畫, in saturated solid indigo, sized to occupy approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Build its geometry from a correct Taiwanese textbook glyph master, preserving all intended joins, openings, and stroke spacing. Initially, every stroke is present except the final bottom horizontal stroke. That last stroke will be drawn during the action; use the master to determine its exact position, thickness, length, and endpoints. Keep the teaching subject centered and uncropped throughout.

The original lead is a proudly determined mint-green rubber dinosaur with enormous soft feet, comically tiny arms, and a bouncy rubber tail. Its only supporting prop is one indigo crayon, lying beside the starting point of the missing bottom stroke. Present the scene as a shallow drawing stage so its feet and the crayon can contact the drawing surface while the lettering remains square to camera.

From 0.0–1.6 seconds, the dinosaur bends toward the crayon, concentrating fiercely. Its tiny arms paddle and miss twice, while its enormous toes are already touching the crayon. It looks from its useless little hands down to its toes and pauses in sudden realization. From 1.6–2.4 seconds, it proudly grips the crayon between two toes and raises its chin like a master artist. From 2.4–3.7 seconds, it presses the tip to the correct starting point and pushes sideways. Its oversized foot slides farther than expected: both tiny arms windmill, its rubber body stretches, and it lands softly on its bottom while the toe-held crayon smoothly completes the exact final horizontal stroke. The controlled crayon trace produces one clean, straight line with no stray marks. Keep this action below the other strokes. A quiet rubber squeak accompanies the landing.

From 3.7–4.8 seconds, the seated dinosaur looks up at the perfectly completed 畫, glances proudly at its giant foot, and gives a delighted tiny-arm victory pose. It scoots out through the right margin, carrying the crayon in its toes. From 4.8–8.0 seconds, hold completely still on the finished glyph alone for 3.2 full seconds. The completed character remains flat, crisp, unobstructed, and unchanged.

Use rounded toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright restrained colors, and a clean composition. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「畫、畫、畫畫」. Pronounce the isolated 畫 at approximately 0.3 and 1.7 seconds, then say the everyday word 畫畫 naturally around 5.5–6.5 seconds while the complete glyph is clearly held. Use the reading ㄏㄨㄚˋ throughout and stop after the word. Keep sound effects gentle and beneath the voice; use no music. Only the single target glyph appears as writing: the vocabulary stays audio only, with no subtitles, extra lettering, logos, watermarks, clutter, or flashing effects.
